title.narrative: Output 4.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop policies, legislation and other measures that are specifically aimed at facilitating the transition of enterprises to formality

description.narrative:
In September 2023, the government of Nigeria through Small and Medium Enterprise Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) in consultation with social partners, the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment as well as other relevant stakeholders, validated and adopted an evidence-based gender-responsive action plan and implementation monitoring framework. The documents developed in July 2023 through consultative workshops with government, social partners, the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment and other relevant stakeholders seeks to foster national conditions for Women’s Entrepreneurship Development (WED and formalization in Nigeria). The Action Plan will contribute towards a more gender-responsive environment for SME development and formalization and greater gender equality within the world of work, unleashing the potential of women’s entrepreneurship and women-led businesses to generate decent jobs in the formal economy at the country level, leading to social inclusion in economic development as well as empowerment of women The Action Plan was developed to implement the findings and key recommendations of two assessments, carried out by Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA) and the government of Nigeria between June and September 2022, in Lagos and Rivers States, namely: (1) National Assessment of the Framework Conditions for WED; and (2) Identification of Barriers and Opportunities to formalize Women-led Small Economic Units in Rivers and Lagos States. The assessments were validated in October 2022 by Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA) and the government of Nigeria during workshops held in Lagos and Abuja With support from the Regular Budget Supplementary Allocation (RBSA) intervention, the ILO in September 2023 supported the government of Nigeria through SMEDAN in collaboration with social partners to convene the validation meeting of the action plan and its implementation monitoring framework. In June 2023, ILO supported the Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA) and the government to engage two consultants who facilitated the development of the action plan and its implementation monitoring framework. The ILO also provided technical guidance on the categories of interventions on which the plan was developed, reviewed, and provided technical inputs into the draft of the above mentioned documents. Later in July 2023, the ILO supported partners to convene workshops and meetings in Lagos and Rivers to discuss the findings of the assessments and validate them as a preliminary step to drafting the action plan.
With support from the same project, the ILO between June – September 2022, supported the Nigeria Employers’ Consultative Association (NECA) and the government of Nigeria to engage three consultants who facilitated the assessment. The ILO also provided technical guidance on the methodology, reviewed, and provided technical inputs into the draft assessment reports to ensure alignment with the WED strategy.
